start: docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md 13.6 design point: spec + chain ladder L1-3 + R-U2..R-U8 (pooled engines, adopted communication levers); HC 5,120 lanes/weight lane at its measured 126-cycle depth
realism: best-shippable packaging (2-die packages, tensor group 4 across a package pair), realistic links (130 ns light-FEC package hop, 10 ns UCIe), reticle-size dies with the stack counts that fit (4 HBM3E stacks per die, 8 per 2-die package: user decision 2026-09-27), block areas inside the die's compute envelope (328.9 mm2, the analytical N5 figure; block areas are ASAP7, so the check is conservative), clocks only where the slowest routed blocks close (or a named retime of the few that do not).  The ladder stops where the next lever would need anything else.

ladder.lever: router || shared expert (drop the one-engine issue edge)
ladder.feasibility: pooled engines (R-U2) put the BF16 router and the FP8 shared expert on different pools; shared_gu's data input is xq only (tools/hdc_golden_v41.py MoE order), so it may start with the router

ladder.lever: router replicated on the 4 dies (no router all-gather)
ladder.feasibility: 3.9 MB/layer of BF16 gate on every die (+0.09% ROM); each die computes all 384 scores (53 cycles on the BF16 pool); was negative in 13.4 only because the router's 4x issue then delayed the shared expert

ladder.lever: 4x BF16 engine on the 4 lm_head dies
ladder.feasibility: the head dies run only the lm_head, argmax and draft rows; 4 x 18.8 mm2 on 4 dies (+56 mm2 in the array) fits their envelope; bytes are ROM-resident, read at 4x the rate (ROM macro capacity 828 KB/cycle vs 2x 36,928 x 2 B = 148 KB/cycle)

ladder.lever: uncapped index scans split over 8 dies (own + neighbour group)
ladder.feasibility: layers 2, 8, 14, 20 only: the neighbour group's indexer pool and HBM are idle while this group scans at batch 1 and do the same total work at any batch; half of the layer's index keys (68 B each) are written to the neighbour's HBM at compression time (capacity: KV lives in 4 of 28 groups, the rest have spare); costs a query hop and one more merge level, 2 x 140 ns

ladder.lever: block-dot pool widened to the HBM key limit
ladder.feasibility: the pooled block-dot engine widened to what the die's stacks can feed (stacks x 0.9 TB/s / 68 B per key x 4,096 MACs a key); with 4 stacks that is 51 keys/cycle, below the pool's 61.6, so the scan is HBM-bound and the lever is empty
a pre-decoded instruction queue issues back to back; the replay (results/arch/v41x_replay.json) found a 1-cycle issue worth 2.7 us; ot_rom_pkg_ctrl closes at 1,162 MHz

ladder.lever: 3-cycle FP add in every stream-op depth (not only the chains)
ladder.feasibility: rtl/hdc/ot_hdc_fastfp.sv (3-cycle add, routed 1,312 MHz, closed) is already the spec's add; the DAG's depth formulas still count 5-cycle adds in each op

ladder.lever: matrix-engine output tree on the 3-cycle add
ladder.feasibility: the same fast add in the weight/BF16 pools' block-sum tree: 4 cycles a level instead of 6

ladder.lever: radix-4 IEEE divider (19 cycles) in normalize / route weights / pool / softplus
ladder.feasibility: measured by the vector-unit agent (docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md 6 item 2: IEEE divide 19 cycles, radix-4), bit-exact IEEE division, so the golden is unchanged

ladder.lever: one Sinkhorn unit per verified position (6 per die)
ladder.feasibility: the MTP verify's 6 positions queue on one ot_hdc_sinkhorn per sublayer engine (6 rounds of ~42 unit clocks x 7 core cycles): 80 of the verify's 235 us at 1M are Sinkhorn; 6 units (33,091 um2 each, +0.2 mm2) run them at once; no effect at batch 1 without MTP

ladder.lever: HC projection widened until the MTP verify is within 0.2% of unlimited HC (1M)
ladder.feasibility: the HC projection stays a separate FP32 unit (~1,169 um2 per lane, fp32 add + mul pipes); once the chain and link levers shorten the sublayer body, its 126-cycle side branch surfaces on the 6-position verify path (spec agent, 2026-09-27); width chosen as the smallest power-of-two multiple of 1,024 lanes per weight lane within 0.2% of unlimited at 1M

ladder.lever: core clock 1.034 -> 1.087 GHz (retime softplus, BF16 MAC, SFU lane)
ladder.feasibility: the next-slowest routed token-path block is ot_hdc_tselect_w16 at 1,087 MHz; the three slower ones (softplus 1,034 closed, the BF16 MAC 1.03-1.05, the SFU lane 1,058 not closed) each take one more register stage (priced: +1 cycle is inside their depth margins); Sinkhorn stays a multicycle path

ladder.lever: pooled engines x2 (block-dot, BF16, vector unit) inside the envelope
ladder.feasibility: 2x the pooled block-dot and BF16 engines and the vector unit: at m = 2 the layer die's blocks are ~246 mm2 ASAP7, inside the 328.9 mm2 N5 compute envelope; the ROM read (2 x 326 KB/cycle) stays under the macros' 828 KB/cycle; the key stream stays at the HBM limit

stop: the ladder stops at the envelope: beyond it are a 4-die package (option c, ~2028+), a sub-100 ns board link (no FEC-free 112G board-reach standard), clocks past the 1,087-1,123 MHz routed blocks (every stream lane, select and link endpoint would need retiming), or the rejected norm folding (changes the FP8 quantisation point)
